redTestChanges.reason: Fixed a resource-cleanup deadlock in the EC-20 test's own finally block, unrelated to any assertion or spec disagreement: `wss.close()`/`server.close()` (built directly by this one test, not via startHarness) never resolve because the client socket this test opens (`owner.socket`) was never closed anywhere before those two awaits, and ws's WebSocketServer.close() (constructed with an externally-owned `server`) only fires its callback once its tracked client count reaches zero rather than proactively terminating clients. Every other test in the file relies on the shared top-level afterEach to close `clients` BEFORE closing its harness's wss/server; this test uniquely closes its own wss/server inside its own try/finally, which completes before that afterEach ever runs. Added one line (`owner?.socket.close();`, first statement of the finally block) plus hoisting the `owner` declaration (`let owner: TestClient | undefined;`) above the try block so it is reachable from finally. No assertion, expectation, or behavioral check was touched. Reproduced and confirmed in isolation before touching the file (see changes.md's Red-test changes section for the full reproduction trace).
